items.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
items.summary: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a…
instructions: Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks.
First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions.
Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a “*” in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored.
Without it, the attack fails.” Company researchers said their testing also showed that the account must be active, not just hold a hash.
